# pysacd-extract: a drop-in replacement for sacd_extract

`pysacd-extract` takes `sacd_extract`'s options and writes the same files,
with the same names and the same bytes.

## Migrating

```sh
ln -s "$(command -v pysacd-extract)" ~/bin/sacd_extract    # that's the whole migration
```

Scripts, `sacd_extract.cfg` (including `logging=1`) and muscle memory keep
working:

```console
$ pysacd-extract -2 -m -s -i album.iso       # DSF, stereo + multichannel
$ pysacd-extract -e -C -i album.iso          # DSDIFF edit master + cue + xml
$ pysacd-extract -P -i album.iso             # disc information, as sacd_extract prints it
$ pysacd-extract -I -s -i 192.0.2.10:2002    # copy a PS3 disc and extract it, one pass over the network
```

Front ends that run `sacd_extract`, such as
[sacd-extract-gui](https://github.com/amstelchen/sacd-extract-gui) and
SACDExtractGUI (its original repository is gone), work unchanged:
point their executable setting at `pysacd-extract`. Programs written in Python
don't need a separate process at all; see [the Python library](library.md).

## Compatibility policy

Differences from `sacd_extract` are treated as bugs. The exceptions below are
deliberate:

| Where | sacd_extract | pysacd-extract | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Two discs aimed at one folder (sets mastered as 1/1, e.g. *Live-Evil*) | mixes them silently, and overwrites tracks whose names match | writes the second disc to `<album> [<catalogue no.>]` and warns; `--disc N/M` gives sacd_extract's own `Disc N` layout | silent mixing is a bug (#4). The discs are told apart by the names and the tags of the files in the folder (album, title, track number and count, ISRC), because `sacd_extract`'s files carry no catalogue number. **A disc for which all of those are equal is taken for the same disc, and its files are replaced, as `sacd_extract` does.** Use a separate `-o` for two masterings of one album |
| Hostile disc text (invisible characters such as controls, bidi and zero-width characters, tag characters or U+2028; `` ` $ ; ``; a leading `-`) | copied into names, tags, cue, XML and `-P` as is | neutralised: invisible characters removed (a control becomes a space) and shown as escapes in `-P`; ordinary discs are unaffected | [security](security.md#hostile-text) |
| A title with nothing usable in it (only dots, spaces or control characters), or one whose trimmed form starts with a dot | uses what its trimming leaves: `..`, `.`, a hidden `.name` or an empty name, so the output can land in the parent of the output folder, in the output folder itself or at the filesystem root | never makes `.`, `..` or a name starting with `.`: a leading `.` becomes `_`, an empty album folder is `Unknown Album`, an empty file name is `_`; and it refuses any path outside the output folder | output must stay inside the output folder ([security](security.md#hostile-text)); ordinary titles are unaffected |
| A relative output folder starting with `./` or `../` (`-o ../out`) | trims the leading dots, which makes it `/out` | uses the folder as given | the folder is the user's choice |
| Malformed TOC timing (a track running past its area's playtime, a zero-length track, more audio than the area's sectors can hold) | uses the times as given: writes a header-only file for a zero-length track and only the frames it finds | cuts tracks to the playtime (so `-P` and the files show the cut times), stops with an error on a zero-length track, on more audio than the image's sectors can hold, or on tracks that together claim that more than twice per format | no real disc does this; a hostile one could ask for hours of output ([security](security.md#hostile-images)) |
| Korean (KSC 5601) and Chinese GB 2312 disc text | written into names, tags and cue sheets as the raw disc bytes, which aren't UTF-8 | decoded, and written as UTF-8 | names that aren't UTF-8 break most tools and can't be written on macOS or Windows. Shift-JIS and Big5 discs, which `sacd_extract` decodes, are byte-identical (`tests/test_names.py`, #47) |
| Raw-sector images (2064/2054 bytes per sector) | refused | read; `-I` writes a plain ISO | real rips exist in that form |
| A dropped PS3 connection | gives up | reconnects and resumes, after checking it's still the same disc | PS3 drives are flaky |
| Running as root | runs | runs, with a one-line warning | `sacd_extract` users run it with `sudo`; [security](security.md#running-as-root) |
| An area whose only missing frame is its last, after DSD silence (#93) | | fills the frame with silence, warns, and exits 0; any other missing frame still makes the exit status 1. **This is a workaround** for what was seen on early Sony discs (Master TOC 1.00, pressed 2000–2001; four discs of four titles), whose last area sector holds no audio sector header. It may be revisited if other discs show the pattern. The frame before it must be DSD silence: in every 384-bit window of every channel, the count of ones is within 2 of half. On the four discs, those frames deviate by at most 1, while sampled music frames have a median of 24 to 27; with DST kept as stored (`-p`, `-e` without `-c`) that can't be tested, and the run fails as before | the audio is complete: the one filled frame (1/75 s) is silence either way |
| An image cut short inside the audio | stops at the cut, writing what it has | reads up to the cut and writes the rest of each track as silence (counted as missing frames, exit status 1), as long as the run's outputs hold more audio than silence, plus 10 seconds; a run that would be mostly silence (say, only tracks past the cut) stops with an error and writes nothing | scarletbook's reading of the specification: positions it can't find are missing frames. The limit keeps a sparse or hole-filled image from turning into gigabytes of silence ([security](security.md#hostile-images)) |
| A DST frame the specification calls invalid (for example a code value out of range, sacd-spec corpus `dst-code-all-ones`) | decodes it anyway, into undefined audio | fills it with 0x55, as for any undecodable frame, warns, and counts it as a DST error (exit status 1) | the frame has no defined audio; since 0.3.0 scarletbook decodes, and it applies the specification's validity rules |
| Unreadable frames in a DSDIFF file that keeps DST (`-p`, `-e` without `-c`) | leaves them out | leaves them out too, and also the markers that would fall past the frames the file holds (a track file's index marker at its end, an edited master's later markers) | since 0.4.0 scarletbook lays out the file for the frames it holds, and a marker can't point past them; only on a damaged image |
| `-b` (pauses) | cuts on sectors, so frames near a boundary can land in both tracks (on one real disc of the five we compare, 6 frames at 4 of its 17 boundaries; with `-z`, the carry then shifts every later track) | cuts on frame timecodes: the tracks joined are exactly the area's audio | gapless and unambiguous |
| DSDIFF "creating machine" comment; `.cue`/`.xml` version lines | name sacd-ripper | name pysacd | honesty; otherwise byte-identical |
| Pad byte after odd-length text and ID3 tags in a DSDIFF file | leaves it uninitialised when DST is kept (or with `-e`), so it holds whatever was in memory | writes zero | the byte has no meaning, and it can't be matched |
| Console messages | | `-P` and the cfg summary are identical; other lines are worded differently | |

## Extensions

Extensions are long options only, so they never collide with `sacd_extract`'s
short ones:

- `--flac`, `--wav`: PCM output, gapless, 24-bit;
- `--musicbrainz`: tags and cover art;
- `--submit-isrcs` (with `--musicbrainz`): offer the disc's ISRCs to the
  matched release, asking first ([details](converting.md#submitting-isrcs-to-musicbrainz));
- `--templates`: your own folder and file naming. A file that already exists is kept and counted
  in a closing "skipped" line; `--overwrite` replaces it. (With `sacd_extract`'s own naming, a
  re-run replaces the files, as `sacd_extract` does.)
- `--threads`;
- `--exact`: for a track far into an area, read the area up to it instead of starting
  provisionally ([why](development.md#the-audio-through-scarletbook));
- `--disc N/M`: place a disc mastered as 1/1 into a set;
- `--log-file`, `--log-level`: see [logging](logging.md).

Run `pysacd-extract --help` for the full list.

## Don't take our word for it

```sh
mkdir a b
(cd a && sacd_extract   -2 -m -s -i ../album.iso)
(cd b && pysacd-extract -2 -m -s -i ../album.iso)
diff -r a b && echo identical
```

**What's checked, and where.** Every pull request runs this comparison on generated discs
(`tests/test_extract_tree.py`): plain DSD, DST and both together, at 2, 5 and 6 channels, in every
`sacd_extract`-compatible mode of `tools/extract_compare.py`, against a `sacd_extract` built from a
pinned commit. Real discs carry far more than a generated one can, so the same tool runs on them by
hand before each release ([releasing](development.md#packaging-and-releases)); CI has no real discs.
The comparison didn't run in CI at all for 0.3.0 to 0.4.3: see the [changelog](../CHANGELOG.md).

On a library of real discs:

- **`-P` disc information:** identical on **99 of 99** plain-SACD images.
- **Output trees:** **28 of 28** end-to-end cases byte-identical. They cover
  every cfg mode, `-o`/`-y`, `-z`, `-k`, `-b`, `-I -w`, 5-channel areas,
  multi-disc sets, titles with trailing spaces, a disc with no text, DSDIFF
  edit masters, cue and XML.
- **DST:** **6,676,925 frames** (27 areas, about 24.7 hours) decoded with no
  errors.
- **Full DST syntax:** every optional feature, forced by a test-only encoder
  at 2, 5 and 6 channels, gives identical results from the original, pysacd
  and `sacd_extract`.
- **PCM:** matches FFmpeg's DSD decoder to −104 dB below 20 kHz. Tracks join
  sample-exactly.

Speed comparisons are in [performance](performance.md).
